title: Worshipping 12-Foot Sacred Crocodiles
hook: In ancient Fayum, priests kept a live Nile crocodile draped in gold earrings and crystal bracelets.

scenes.text: To the ancient Egyptians, the Nile crocodile wasn't just a deadly river predator—it was the living embodiment of Sobek, god of fertility and power.

scenes.text: In the city of Crocodilopolis, priests handpicked one sacred crocodile called Petsuchos to live in a luxurious temple lake.

scenes.text: Priests pierced its ears with gold and turquoise earrings, and fitted its forelegs with sparkling crystal and electrum bracelets.

scenes.text: Visiting Greek tourists like Strabo watched in awe as priests pried open the giant reptile's jaws to feed it cakes, roasted meat, and honey wine.
